authorityReview.evidence: Only the inherited two-argument nonpayable mint(address _recipient,uint256 _mintAmount) is admitted. It runs nonReentrant and settleInterest; Base._mintInternal invokes the configured controller's beforeMint, computes an exchange rate, then the inherited iToken _doTransferIn uses the configured underlying token's safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, iToken, amount). It computes minted iTokens from actual received assets and the exchange rate, mints to the caller-selected _recipient, checks the total-supply threshold, calls controller.afterMint, and emits Mint. The controller, underlying token, exchange-rate/interest model, balances, allowance, totals, threshold, and market conditions are protocol dependencies that may reject or revert. The source's separate concrete iTokenV2BLP three-argument mint(address,uint256,bool) only adds optional refreshEligibility behavior; that ABI is distinct and excluded. Platform policy imposes no amount, recipient, recipient/owner-equality, balance, oracle, or financial gate; zero or other ABI-valid arguments and full uint256 values remain caller-selected and may fail protocol checks. Underlying-token approval is independent and is neither paired nor granted here.

Only the inherited two-argument nonpayable redeem(address _from,uint256 _redeemiToken) is admitted. It runs nonReentrant and settleInterest, computes the underlying amount through the interest-dependent exchange rate, and enters Base._redeemInternal. The body rejects zero shares, calls the configured controller beforeRedeem, burns from caller-selected _from (the inherited ERC20 _burnFrom requires allowance when _from differs from msg.sender), enforces the total-supply threshold, then calls _doTransferOut(msg.sender, amount) and controller.afterRedeem. The iTokenV2 override of _doTransferOut calls configured controller.beforeTransferUnderlying(iToken, configuredUnderlying, amount, msg.sender), receives _dst, and safe-transfers the underlying to that returned destination. Therefore msg.sender is supplied to the hook, but the final payout destination is controller-selected; no claim is made that redeem always pays the caller or _from. Controller routing/permission/accounting, underlying token, exchange rate and interest, _from balance/allowance, total-supply threshold, available market cash, and protocol conditions may redirect or revert the operation. The concrete iTokenV2BLP three-argument redeem(address,uint256,bool) adds optional refreshEligibility and is distinct/excluded. Platform policy imposes no _from/owner or recipient restriction, share-amount cap, balance, oracle, or financial gate; zero and all uint256 ABI values remain caller-selected and may be rejected by protocol logic. No separate approval is paired or granted. Dated source evidence and this two-method admission do not prove current controller routing, underlying configuration, market liquidity, funded execution, a complete workflow, or financial safety.
